 Woman Complains About Rejected FAS Application, Man Calls Out Her Previous $1,066 Spending On BTS Tickets
 Plan B 2 hours ago 2 min read A Singaporean netizen, @muhdnoor.asmain, has sparked an online debate after calling out a Threads user who claimed to have spent S$1,066 on BTS concert tickets, despite also sharing that her application for the Ministry of Education's Financial Assistance Scheme (FAS) had been unsuccessful. 
 In his post, he shared screenshots of user @allasamz, who had expressed frustration over her rejected FAS application and the lack of response from her child's school regarding school-based financial assistance. 
 However, he questioned her spending priorities after discovering another post in which she mentioned spending S$1,066 on BTS tickets. 
 His post drew widespread agreement from netizens, many of whom felt that parents should prioritise their children's educational necessities over luxuries. 
 Some also highlighted the user's previous posts about travelling to Korea and enquiring about a private Mount Fuji tour in Japan, further questioning her financial priorities. 
 Joining the discussion, verified Threads user @shakirahfiraz suggested that the issue was not necessarily about exploiting the system, but rather the perceived insensitivity of publicly displaying an expensive lifestyle while complaining about a rejected financial assistance application. 
 However, others defended the user, arguing that being able to afford concert tickets or travel does not necessarily mean someone is financially comfortable. 
 They pointed out that such expenses could have been saved for over time and that parents should not be judged for occasionally rewarding themselves, particularly if they meet the scheme's eligibility criteria. 
 The discussion also raised concerns over the FAS application and appeals process, with some questioning its fairness. 
 Others shared experiences of being denied assistance despite financial struggles, while one netizen recalled helping a family with school expenses, only to later see them flaunting luxury purchases. 
 Under MOE'S FAS, Singapore Citizen students qualify if their family's gross monthly household income is S$4,000 or below, or their monthly per capita household income is S$1,000 or below. 
 The scheme covers school fees, textbooks, uniforms and other essential school expenses, with additional support for meals and transport.
